overview: DOSER proposes a framework for offline reinforcement learning that uses diffusion models to detect out-of-distribution actions via reconstruction error and selectively regularizes them by classifying into beneficial or detrimental categories using a learned dynamics model to balance conservatism and exploration.

modules.name: Offline Dataset Processing
modules.description: Handles loading of offline reinforcement learning datasets (e.g., D4RL), standardizing observation and action spaces, and constructing a replay buffer for efficient sampling of state-action-reward-next_state quadruples.

modules.name: EDM Diffusion Framework Core
modules.description: Implements the foundational Elucidating Diffusion Model (EDM) components, including continuous-time noise scheduling, stochastic differential equation solvers, network preconditioning (skip connections and scaling), and the denoising score matching loss function.

modules.name: Behavior Policy Diffusion Model
modules.description: Constructs the conditional diffusion model for approximating the empirical behavior policy, taking noisy actions and state conditions as input to predict the original clean actions, trained via the reweighted L2 reconstruction objective.

modules.name: State Distribution Diffusion Model
modules.description: Constructs the unconditional diffusion model for capturing the state distribution of the offline dataset, taking noisy states as input to predict the original clean states, used to measure the conformity of next states.

modules.name: Reconstruction-based OOD Detection
modules.description: Computes the single-step denoising reconstruction error for both actions and states, and determines the OOD indicator by comparing the error against a statistical threshold (p-th percentile of in-sample errors).

modules.name: Dynamics Model Learning
modules.description: Implements the supervised training of a deterministic dynamics model to predict next states and rewards given current state-action pairs, serving as the transition function for evaluating OOD action outcomes.

modules.name: OOD Action Classification Logic
modules.description: Integrates the dynamics model, state OOD detector, and value estimates to classify OOD actions into 'beneficial' or 'detrimental' sets based on whether the predicted next state is in-distribution and yields a higher value than the optimal in-distribution action.

modules.name: Value and Critic Networks
modules.description: Implements the Value (V) network trained with expectile regression and the Q-network trained with a modified Bellman error that incorporates the OOD action classification logic, applying either a lower-bound penalty for detrimental actions or a value-difference bonus for beneficial actions.

modules.name: Policy Network
modules.description: Implements the actor network with a Tanh-Gaussian architecture, optimized via maximum entropy reinforcement learning objectives to maximize the adjusted Q-values while maintaining exploration.

modules.name: DOSER Training Pipeline
modules.description: Orchestrates the complete training workflow, managing the pretraining phases for diffusion and dynamics models, followed by the iterative reinforcement learning loop where batches are sampled, actions classified, and V/Q/Policy networks updated sequentially according to Algorithm 1.

modules.name: OOD Detection Baselines
modules.description: Implements alternative OOD detection mechanisms for comparison, including Model Ensemble variance, MC Dropout uncertainty estimation, and CVAE-based reconstruction error, providing a standardized interface for evaluation.

modules.name: Benchmark Evaluation Suite
modules.description: Executes policy evaluation in the environment, computes normalized scores against D4RL baselines, and generates visual diagnostics such as t-SNE embeddings of action distributions, Q-value histograms, and OOD error density plots.

modules.name: Ablation and Sensitivity Framework
modules.description: Manages experiment configurations for ablation studies (e.g., removing action classification or value compensation) and performs sensitivity analysis across hyperparameters like OOD detection thresholds, penalty coefficients, and compensation weights.
